headline: The core moved; the long tail did not. The more central the article, the more its opening paragraph changed.
unit: of the Top-importance Israel, Palestine and Jewish-topic articles gained critical vocabulary in their opening paragraph since July 2023; other conflict regions 4.4%
body: Mid importance: 1.5% against none. Low-importance and ungraded pages, about 80% of the 49,000 topic articles, moved no more than elsewhere; across all of them the gap is 0.4 points, within the margin of error. Articles on Judaism did not move. The wave ran through 2024, about 16 new critical terms per 1,000 edits against about 7 before the war, and was back to 5 to 6 by 2026.
compare_label: Top importance: topic vs other conflict regions

headline: [[q|Israel began committing genocide.]] Two of the most-read opening sections now say it in Wikipedia’s own voice.
unit: sentences charging Israel with genocide in the 150 most-read opening sections: Jan 2021, Jul 2023, now (5 Nov 2026)
body: The two in Wikipedia’s own voice are the articles on Israel and on Benjamin Netanyahu. In the Israel article the next sentence is [[q|Israel has denied that its actions constitute genocide.]] Five others attribute the charge; the eighth is the denial. No sentence charges Hamas or Palestinians with genocide.

headline: Occupation became fact, for Israel and for Russia alike.
unit: of occupation charges against Israel stated in Wikipedia’s own voice, 2021 to now
body: Occupation charged to Russia in Crimea and to Turkey in northern Cyprus went from 25% to 74%. Since the July 2024 ICJ advisory opinion, editors have a court to cite. The share of harm sentences naming Israel as the one doing harm barely moved: 23.6% to 26.4%, not statistically clear.

headline: “Militant” left Hamas’s definition. Hamas is now [[q|a Sunni Islamist Palestinian nationalist political organisation with a military wing]].
unit: 19:12 UTC, in the month the Hamas article was read 8,236,474 times
body: “Terrorist” was written into the definition five times; none lasted a day. The designation sentence moved from sentence 5 of 20 (2021) to 22 of 23 (Oct 2026). Neither the Hamas nor the Israel opening section mentions the hostages.

headline: 1948 got an agent. The Nakba is now [[q|the ethnic cleansing of Palestinian Arabs by Zionists]], in Wikipedia’s own voice.
unit: of sentences about Palestinian victims that name no perpetrator, 2021 to now (150 most-read articles)
body: The exodus of Jews from Arab states is still written with no agent: [[q|Hundreds of thousands of Jews fled or were expelled from Arab states]].

headline: Off-wiki canvassing is documented on both sides. The surge came before the Discord channel.
unit: topic insertions of critical terms against comparison, in the 16 weeks after 7 Oct 2023; 2.0× while the channel was active
body: Wikipedia’s arbitration committee found pro-Israel email canvassing (January 2024) and sanctioned editing after off-wiki canvassing on a pro-Palestinian Discord channel (December 2024, April 2025).[[verify|ArbCom items read from search snippets only; check primary pages (ORGS.md section 5)]] In our data, two small groups of four long-standing accounts moved together on the same articles beyond chance (14 linked pairs, where chance gives about 2). None edited in step, no wording was pasted across articles, and their timing matches neither documented window clearly. Our footprint tests could only have seen very large effects.
